newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ jury out for second day in U.K. surgeon's trial.
newsitem.headline: NZ jury out for second day in U.K. surgeon's trial.

text.p: A New Zealand jury failed to reach a verdict for the second day on Wednesday in the trial of a British surgeon accused of manslaughter over the deaths of three patients, a court official said.
The jury of six men and six women spent five hours on Tuesday and all of Wednesday weighing evidence in the case of former surgeon Keith Douglas Ramstead, 44.

The British heart and lung surgeon has pleaded not guilty to the manslaughter of three patients on whom he operated for lung cancer while working as a cardio-thoracic surgeon in New Zealand in 1991 and 1992.
He also denied two charges of making false statements about two of the deaths.
At one point on Wednesday, the jurors returned to the courtroom to ask the judge for clarification of several points.
Justice Anthony Ellis defined manslaughter as an action but for which the patients would not have died, adding there was no difference between medical and criminal manslaughter.
In response to another question, he said the jury must decide whether Ramstead had used reasonable skill, knowledge and care.
The jury was to resume deliberations on Thursday.
During the four-week trial, the prosecution said Ramstead showed criminal negligence in the deaths on the operating table of two men, aged 50 and 74, and an elderly woman.
The defence said there was no evidence that the Liverpool doctor was incompetent and argued the prosecution's case was fundamentally flawed because its theories ignored the facts.
Ramstead eventually returned voluntarily to stand trial in New Zealand after extraditon proceedings lasting 2-1/2 years.
The trial involved detailed testimony of numerous medical professionals for both the prosecution and defence, with often conflicting views on crucial details of the operations.
